statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). The gap-down open is now fully absorbed. NQ front month is quoted at 29,036.00, down 1.19%, holding roughly 74% of the 28,816.25-29,111.00 session range, while the Nasdaq-100 cash index at 29,055.30 trades near 91% of its own 28,867.67-29,074.11 range. VIX is at 17.32, the bottom of its 17.17-18.17 range; the 10-year has retreated from 5.012% to 4.977% and WTI from $104.79 to $103.45. Tail eases one point to 20. The unresolved Saudi East-West pipeline outage remains the outstanding amplifier.
recommendation: Tail at 20 sits at the lower edge of the watch band, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 19:00-20:00 UTC, covering the final cash hour, where conditional Tail peaks at 23, two points below the block mapping. The conditional path eases into the low band across the post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, returns to the watch band during Tuesday's European midday, and reaches 22 for the 12:15 UTC ADP and 12:30 UTC Empire State releases and the 13:30 UTC cash open. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Absorption holds and the amplifiers roll over: NDX presses 91% of its session range while VIX sits at its low, the 10-year retreats from 5.012% and WTI backs off $104.79; Tail eases to 20 with the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour retained as the danger window
body:
The recovery recorded an hour ago has extended rather than faded, and for the first time today all three cross-asset amplifiers are easing at the same time as the index holds its gains. As of the 15:16 UTC quote, NQ front month is at 29,036.00, down 351.00 points or 1.19% against a 29,387.00 reference, with the session range unchanged at 28,816.25 to 29,111.00. Price sits about 220 points above the low, roughly 74% of the range. The cash index is stronger still: the Nasdaq-100 is at 29,055.30, down 1.07%, against a 28,867.67 low and a 29,074.11 high, which places it near 91% of its session range after opening at 28,890.93 on a 1.63% gap. The 28,816.25 futures low has now survived more than five hours spanning the European session, the cash open and two full cash hours. That is a completed, durable retracement rather than the repeated extension after failed pullbacks that defines a pathological path.

The cross-asset picture has turned from amplifying to stabilising. VIX is quoted at 17.32, still up 9.34% against a 15.84 close, but trading at the very bottom of its 17.17 to 18.17 session range; implied volatility that spikes into a gap-down open and then decays through the first two cash hours is the signature of an orderly liquidity transfer. The 10-year Treasury yield printed 5.012% earlier today, its first touch of 5% since October 2023, and has since retreated to 4.977%, the lower end of a 4.973% to 5.012% range, with the 5-year at 4.802% off a 4.840% high. Crude has done the same: WTI reached $104.79 and Brent $109.44 during the European afternoon, and both have since eased to $103.45 and $108.25. An amplifier that fails to extend after making its high is no longer adding to the probability of a no-retracement path.

The catalyst stack itself is unchanged and remains verified. The National reports that Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which normally routes roughly seven million barrels a day from the Eastern Province to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, is still shut after multiple attacks in the Riyadh and Madinah regions on 10 September, with Yanbu holding only five to seven days of export inventory and an estimated 4% of global supply at risk if it is not reopened. Separately, Reuters reports that calls from the heads of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI for a slower pace of AI model development have driven the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down roughly 6%, its worst day since 1 July, with Nvidia off 3.2% and Intel, AMD and Marvell down 5.6%, 5% and 6.3%.

That semiconductor damage is exactly why the index is not trending. The same Reuters report notes healthcare and consumer staples each up about 1% and software higher, with ServiceNow, Adobe and Workday gaining 3.8%, 3.6% and 3.2%. The shared cross-asset context file, collected at 14:26 UTC and therefore fresh, carried a partial collection status with an unavailable calendar section but complete and healthy breadth, megacap, semiconductor and futures sections; used only as confirmation, it shows the same split, with the semiconductor basket averaging -4.72% and every one of its seven members negative, while four of eight megacaps are positive and Communication Services and both software industries are green against Technology at -2.14%. The calendar section was unusable, so the seven-day event list was verified independently. A market in which one industry is down 6% and another is up 3% is dispersing risk internally, not compressing it into a single direction, and that dispersion belongs in Stress rather than Tail.

The remaining live risks are genuine but they are event risks, not path risks. The pipeline outage is unresolved and physical, so a fresh Gulf headline could reprice crude at any hour. Market-implied odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase on Wednesday are reported near 90%, an unusual configuration that keeps the bond market as the dominant cross-asset channel into midweek. Consistent with the published risk definitions, event importance, surprise magnitude and an unresolved supply mechanism raise Stress and discipline Confidence rather than forcing Tail higher once the observed path shows orderly discovery. Tail therefore eases one point to 20 and Stress one point to 75, still in the high band.

The danger window stays at 19:00 to 20:00 UTC, the final cash hour, which is the remaining scheduled point at which a gap-down day either confirms absorption into the settlement or gives it back, and the moment when a late crude headline would meet the thinnest liquidity of the cash session. Conditional Tail peaks at 23 there, two points below the block mapping, reflecting a scheduled transition and the live amplifier count rather than any observed closing structure. Confidence is 89: price, volatility, rates, energy, catalyst and calendar evidence is current and verified from primary sources, with the 2-year yield the one remaining gap.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series ran through the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band from 21:00 UTC as the AI-slowdown and Middle East supply stories developed, and reached the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows into 28,816.25 under a trend-down mode. It stepped back to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, returned to the elevated band at 13:00 UTC when the bounce faded into the cash open, then eased to the watch band at 14:00 UTC as the gap began to be absorbed. Stress held in the high band throughout, between 70 and 79, and Confidence improved from 85 to 88 as live price evidence became available. All 24 hourly slots are available from published Claude history.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built on an opening gap that has been absorbed for two consecutive cash hours while VIX, the 10-year and crude all retreat from their session extremes. Conditional Tail holds at 20 through the second cash hour, eases to 19 across the US midday, and peaks at 23 in the 19:00 UTC power hour that forms the published danger window. It then decays into the low band from 21:00 UTC across the thin post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, with small uplifts in the hours where crude has typically repriced first on Middle East developments. The path returns to the watch band during Tuesday's European midday and US pre-market and reaches 22 for the 12:15 UTC ADP and 12:30 UTC Empire State releases and the 13:30 UTC cash open, two points below the block mapping. Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last verified price observation. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not observed structure.
